# AI speak patterns, part 2

Built from the packs in `hooks/lib/patterns`. Each section names its own source.

The category index is in `ai-speak-patterns.md`.

## overgeneralization

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing and WikiProject AI Cleanup catchphrases.

A universal claim about people or the industry with no source.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `everyone agrees`, `everyone knows`, `everyone understands` | name who agrees |
| `everybody agrees`, `everybody knows` | name who agrees |
| `no one deny`, `no one denies`, `no one can deny`, `no one can denies` | name the source |
| `in every case`, `instance`, `scenario`, `situation` | name the case |
| `the industry agrees`, `the industry is unanimous` | name who agrees |
| `universally acknowledged`, `universally accepted`, `universally recognized`, `universally true` | name who accepts it |
| `without exception` | name the exception, or cut |
| `all developers agree`, and the same verbs after `users`, `teams`, `companies`, `engineers` | name who |
| `every single one`, `every single time`, `every single user`, `every single developer`, `every single case` | cut single, or count |

Bare always, never, and all stay unflagged: they are correct in API docs and code comments. Only a universal claim about a human population is reported.

## paragraph-coherence

Presets: `ryan`, `statistical`, `all`.

Flags formulaic paragraphs: near-identical lengths, repeated opening words, or repeated topic sentences.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags formulaic paragraphs: near-identical lengths, repeated opening words, or repeated topic sentences. | `minWords = 300`, `minParagraphs = 4`, `minParagraphWords = 20`, `minRepeatParagraphs = 5`, `maxLengthCv = 0.15`, `firstWordShare = 0.6`, `minFirstWordCount = 3`, `maxSimilarity = 0.6`, `minPairs = 2` |

Three proxies, any one of which reports on its own: length uniformity, first-word repetition, topic-sentence overlap.

## parallel-bullets

Presets: `ryan`, `all`. Source: Pangram signs-of-ai-writing bullet counts and tropes.fyi bold-first bullets and anaphora abuse.

A bulleted list where every item shares one rigid shape.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| A bulleted list where every item shares one rigid shape. | `minItems = 3`, `minScore = 2`, `strongWeight = 2`, `lengthSpread = 1`, `lengthMinItems = 4` |

A bold lead-in or one shared opening word across every item is enough on its own. The two weaker shapes need a second one.

## passive-voice

Presets: `ryan`, `statistical`, `all`.

Flags text where passive voice runs past a third of the sentences.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags text where passive voice runs past a third of the sentences. | `minWords = 150`, `minSentences = 8`, `maxRatio = 0.3` |

Be-verb plus past participle, counted per sentence. Adjectival forms such as "is committed" are the known false positive.

## promotional

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch (peacock terms) and Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing.

Marketing language for a technical change.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `unlocks the full potential`, `unlock value` | name what changes |
| `supercharge`, `supercharges`, `supercharged` | improve, or name the effect |
| `effortless`, `effortlessly` | simple, or name the steps |
| `legendary`, `iconic`, `visionary` | cut, or cite the achievement |
| `acclaimed`, `celebrated`, `award-winning` | name the award |
| `industry-leading` | name the metric |
| `outstanding` as praise, as in `outstanding work` | name the metric |
| `landmark`, `next-level`, `top-tier`, `turnkey` | name the change |
| `one-stop shop` | say what it does |
| `take it to the next level` | state the improvement |

`outstanding` reports only in a praise frame, so the plain technical sense in `outstanding requests` stays clean.

## punctuation-patterns

Presets: `statistical`, `all`.

Flags punctuation habits that agree: colon and semicolon rate, no exclamations, a uniform Oxford comma, no sentence-initial conjunctions.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags punctuation habits that agree: colon and semicolon rate, no exclamations, a uniform Oxford comma, no sentence-initial conjunctions. | `minWords = 150`, `colonRate = 0.15`, `semicolonRate = 0.1`, `exclamationWords = 300`, `oxfordMin = 6`, `conjunctionSentences = 20`, `minScore = 4` |

Each sub-signal is weak alone. The pack reports only when four of the five agree.

## rare-words

Presets: `statistical`, `all`.

Flags text with an unusually high share of long, low-frequency words.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags text with an unusually high share of long, low-frequency words. | `minWords = 150`, `maxRatio = 0.25`, `minSyllables = 3`, `minLength = 7` |

A length and syllable proxy for register inflation. The vocabulary pack covers the specific words with corpus evidence.

## readability-grade

Presets: `ryan`, `statistical`, `all`.

Flags text with a Flesch-Kincaid grade level above what technical writing needs.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags text with a Flesch-Kincaid grade level above what technical writing needs. | `minWords = 150`, `minSentences = 5`, `maxGrade = 16` |

Flesch-Kincaid grade level over the whole text. It reads register, and says nothing about who wrote the text.

## rule-of-three

Presets: `ryan`, `all`. Source: Pangram signs-of-ai-writing triad counts and tropes.fyi directory.

Triads of adjectives, nouns, or clauses used past the point of restraint.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Triads of adjectives, nouns, or clauses used past the point of restraint. | `minWords = 100`, `minTriads = 3`, `minPerParagraph = 2`, `bulletMaxWords = 8`, `bulletSpread = 3` |

One accurate triad passes. The pack counts triads across the whole text and reports once when the rate crosses the threshold.

## sentence-variation

Presets: `ryan`, `statistical`, `all`.

Flags text where every sentence runs about the same length.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags text where every sentence runs about the same length. | `minWords = 160`, `minSentences = 8`, `minCv = 0.35` |

Sentence-length burstiness, the coefficient of variation of words per sentence.

Word choices from Simplified Technical English.

|---|---|
| `accomplish`, `perform`, `conduct a test`, `conduct the check`, `conduct a review` | do |
| `acquire`, `obtain`, `procure` | get |
| `adhere to`, `comply with` | obey |

| `desire`, `desires`, `desired` | want |
| `indicate`, `indicates`, `indicated` | show |
| `locate`, `locates`, `located` | find |
| `modify`, `modifies`, `modified` | change |
| `observe`, `observes`, `observed` | look at, see |
| `permit`, `permits`, `permitted` | let |
| `purchase`, `purchases`, `purchased` | buy |
| `rectify`, `rectifies`, `rectified`, `remedy`, `remedies`, `remedied` | correct, repair |
| `replenish`, `replenishes`, `replenished` | fill |
| `retain`, `retains`, `retained` | keep |
| `transmit`, `transmits`, `transmitted` | send |
| `verify`, `verifies`, `verified` | make sure |
| `aperture` | hole |
| `malfunction` | fault |
| `personnel` | persons |
| `portion` | part |
| `remainder` | the other part |
| `requirement`, `requirements` | need |
| `termination` | end |
| `utilization` | use |
| `adequate`, `sufficient` | enough |
| `adjacent` | near, next to |
| `approximately` | about |
| `additional` | more |
| `initial` | first |
| `numerous`, `multiple` | many |
| `optimum` | best |
| `previous` | before, earlier |
| `principal` | main |
| `ensure` | make sure |
| `examine`, `inspect` | do a check of |
| `vicinity` | area |
| `rapidly` | quickly |
| `subsequent` | after, next |

Off unless the preset is `ste` or `all`. The rules behind the list are in `simplified-technical-english.md`.

## structure

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Openers and frames that delay the point.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `What does this mean`, `So why should you care`, `Why does it matter` as an opener | answer it |
| `Picture this.`, `Run the numbers.`, `Think about it.`, `Consider this:` as a line-initial fragment | state the fact |
| `Three key takeaways`, `5 things to know`, `Four reasons`, `10 ways`, `Six tips` (line-initial) | drop the count, lead with the finding |
| `Let me think step by step`, `Let me break this down step by step`, `Let me walk through this step by step`, `Here's my thought process`, `To approach this systematically`, `Breaking this down:` | cut, give the result |
| `Enter Redis.` and the rest of the reveal form | name it in a plain sentence |
| `ever wondered`, `have you ever wondered`, `what if I told you` | state the fact |
| `Imagine a world where`, `Picture a future in which`, `Envision a scenario where` | state the fact |
| `You're asking about`, `To answer your question`, `The question of whether` (sentence-initial) | answer |

## superficial-analysis

Presets: `ryan`, `all`. Source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing and tropes.fyi directory.

A significance claim with no evidence behind it.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `this is important because`, `this matters because` | state the fact |
| `has significant implications for`, `has significant implications on` | name the implication |
| `cannot be overstated`, `can't be overstated` | state the fact plainly |
| `underscores its importance`, `underscores its significance` | state the fact |
| `goes a long way toward`, `goes a long way in`, `goes a long way to` | cut, state the result |
| `speaks volumes about` | state the fact |
| `carries significant weight`, `carries considerable weight`, `carries real weight` | name the weight, or cut |
| `highlighting its importance` | state the fact, drop the tail |

## sycophancy

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `minimal`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Praise aimed at the reader instead of the work.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `You're right` (sentence-initial) | cut, state the fix |
| `you're absolutely right` | cut |
| `what a great`, `what a fantastic`, `what a wonderful` | cut |
| `Great point`, `Great idea`, `Great catch`, `Excellent observation`, `Excellent suggestion` | cut |
| `That's a great point`, `That's an excellent point`, `That's a fantastic idea`, `That's a really good observation`, `That's an insightful observation` | cut |
| `I completely understand`, `I completely agree`, `I totally understand`, `I totally agree` | cut |
| `thank you for sharing`, `thank you for bringing this`, `thank you for pointing`, `thank you for the clarification`, `thank you for your patience` | cut |
| `thanks for sharing`, `thanks for pointing`, `thanks for flagging` | cut |
| `You raise a great point`, `You raise an excellent point`, `You raise a good point`, `You raise a valid point`, `You raise an important point` | cut |
| `I apologize for the confusion`, `I apologize for the oversight`, `I apologize for the inconvenience`, `I apologize for any confusion`, `I apologize for any oversight`, `I apologize for any inconvenience`, `apologies for the confusion`, `my apologies` | state the correction |

## terminal-punctuation

Presets: `statistical`, `all`.

Flags list items that all carry a trailing period even though they read as short fragments.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags list items that all carry a trailing period even though they read as short fragments. | `minWords = 0`, `minItems = 8`, `minBlocks = 2`, `maxItemWords = 8` |

List items only. Every declarative sentence ends in a period, so sentence-level uniformity carries no signal.

## transition-density

Presets: `ryan`, `statistical`, `all`.

Flags text where too many sentences open on a transition or connector word.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags text where too many sentences open on a transition or connector word. | `minWords = 150`, `minSentences = 8`, `maxDensity = 0.3` |

Document-wide connector rate. The transitions pack flags single openers; this one flags the habit.

## transitions

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Connectors and scene setters that add length without adding a fact.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Moreover`, `Furthermore`, `Additionally` (sentence-initial) | cut, or "and", "also" |
| `Notably`, `Importantly`, `Interestingly`, `Surprisingly` (sentence-initial) | cut |
| `in today's` | name the context or cut |
| `in an era where`, `in an era of` | cut |
| `in the evolving world of`, `in the evolving field of`, `in the changing world of`, `in the changing field of`, `in the rapidly evolving world of`, `in the rapidly evolving field of`, `in the rapidly changing world of`, `in the rapidly changing field of` | lead with the point |
| `worth noting`, `it's worth noting`, `it is worth noting` | state the fact |
| `when it comes to` | name the thing |
| `here's what's interesting`, `here's what caught my eye`, `here's what stood out`, `here's the interesting part` | state the fact |
| `that said`, `that being said` | cut, or "but" |
| `Certainly`, `Undoubtedly`, `Without a doubt` | cut |
